top_categories.workout_context: 10,023ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Cycle to the Sun — Haleakala's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
36 miles on paved Hawaiian volcanic mountain road burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
At Cycle to the Sun — Haleakala, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
10,023ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Base fitness for Cycle to the Sun — Haleakala. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.
278ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.

Road-specific control matters at Cycle to the Sun — Haleakala. Practice on paved Hawaiian volcanic mountain road: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 36 miles.
Low-cadence force work supports 10,023ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Cycle to the Sun — Haleakala. Train it until it feels boring.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on paved Hawaiian volcanic mountain road can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Cycle to the Sun — Haleakala. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.

race_overlay.heat: June in Pa'ia, Maui, Hawaii can bring heat. Complete 3–4 heat exposure sessions in the final 2 weeks before Cycle to the Sun — Haleakala. Increase sodium intake 48 hours before race day.
race_overlay.nutrition: Use training to rehearse an eating and drinking plan that matches the ride duration, intensity, and weather. Use the organizer's current resupply plan for final carry decisions.
race_overlay.altitude: Cycle to the Sun — Haleakala includes meaningful altitude exposure. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing. 40-degree Fahrenheit temperature drop from start to summit; Summit wind chill can feel below freezing even in summer.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on VO2max, Race Simulation, and Durability to prepare you for 36 miles of paved hawaiian volcanic mountain road in Pa'ia, Maui, Hawaii.
